title: What the City’s own reviewers wrote about these exceptions
question: What have the Controller, the Board’s budget analyst and the civil grand jury said in writing about emergency purchasing, waivers and sole-source contracts?
finding: 10 reports from 2012 to 2026 address these routes directly, 6 of them since 2024. The same criticism recurs: a waiver granted because a competition was not planned in time. The budget analyst wrote in 2012 that the Health Department “extends sole source contracts beyond their initial terms”; the Controller wrote in 2024 that “poor planning for procurements is not an appropriate justification”; and the Health Department’s own fiscal 2024-25 list gives time to run a competition as the reason for 23 of its 28 waivers.
how: Reports in the project’s document library by the Controller, the Budget and Legislative Analyst and the Civil Grand Jury were searched for the words emergency procurement, sole source, waiver and no-bid, and the ten that make a finding about one of these routes were read. Each row gives the publisher’s date, a one-sentence summary, a quotation of at most twelve words checked against the stored text, and the link recorded when the document was downloaded.
limits: These are findings about particular departments in particular years, not about every use of an exception, and several departments have since changed their procedures; the Controller’s follow-up reports record which recommendations were carried out. A short quotation cannot carry a report’s reasoning: read the page it comes from. The library holds what this project collected, not every report ever issued.

rows.document: The Office of the Treasurer & Tax Collector Improperly Steered Contracts to the Former Chief Assistant Treasurer’s Friend’s Company
rows.said: The Controller found that the Treasurer and Tax Collector’s office paid one firm for a new project through another firm’s existing sole-source contract, work it would otherwise have had to put out to bid.
rows.quote: “arrangement was wholly improper because TTX used this sole source contract”

rows.document: At Scale, At Risk: Upgrading Data and Oversight to Improve Homelessness Services (Civil Grand Jury 2025-26)
rows.said: The civil grand jury recorded that the Board in March 2024 extended the waiver of bidding for homelessness contracts from May 2024 to May 2029.
rows.quote: “No-bid, streamlined contracting allows HSH to bypass the months-long competitive solicitation process”

rows.publisher: San Francisco Budget and Legislative Analyst
rows.said: The budget analyst found that a $5.9 million one-year permit-software contract was awarded on a software waiver without competition, nearly eight times the size of the average new-software waiver, and counted 68 such waivers worth $97.1 million approved in fiscal 2024-25.

rows.publisher: San Francisco Budget and Legislative Analyst
rows.document: Performance Audit of the Procurement of Public Works Contracts Under Chapter 6 of the Administrative Code by Public Works, the Airport, the Port, Recreation and Parks, and Municipal Transportation Agency
rows.said: The budget analyst found that the Port had no written procedures for sole-source or emergency public-works procurement although it used both during the audit period.

rows.document: Human Rights Commission: Audit of purchasing, grants and Prop Q compliance
rows.said: The Controller found that 93% of the $2.6 million of small purchases it reviewed at the Human Rights Commission, made under the rule that lets a department buy without bids, were ineligible or likely ineligible for that rule.

rows.document: Public Integrity Review: Criminal Conduct by Former SFPUC GM Harlan Kelly Undermined the Integrity of City Procurements Despite Existing Rules Governing Gifts, Disclosures, and Sole Source Waivers
rows.said: The Controller found that the Public Utilities Commission obtained a sole-source waiver for holiday lights on reasoning that showed it had not planned the purchase, and recommended that the Office of Contract Administration spell out what does not justify a waiver.
rows.quote: “poor planning for procurements is not an appropriate justification”

rows.document: Time to Get to Work: San Francisco’s Hiring Crisis
rows.said: The civil grand jury found that the City over-uses temporary positions that are exempt from civil-service hiring, and recommended a yearly audit of them.
rows.quote: “The City continues to over-utilize temporary exempt positions”

rows.document: Public Integrity Review: Preliminary Assessment of San Francisco Public Works Contracting
rows.said: The Controller found that Public Works awarded 15 contracts worth $24.6 million under the homelessness waiver and 6 worth $3.2 million under emergency powers, without the controls needed to ensure fair selection, and recommended citywide procedures for both.
rows.quote: “needed controls over such solicitations were lacking in Public Works”

rows.publisher: San Francisco Budget and Legislative Analyst
rows.document: Board of Supervisors Role in Emergency Response
rows.said: The budget analyst noted that the coronavirus emergency had already run for months, that the Mayor directs the response for as long as it lasts, and that the Board could take a larger part in decisions about recovery.
rows.quote: “the Mayor is empowered to direct the City’s administrative response”

rows.publisher: San Francisco Budget and Legislative Analyst
rows.document: Professional Services Contracts: Dept of Public Health & Human Services Agency
rows.said: The budget analyst found that the Health Department awarded 22% of its professional-services contract value in fiscal 2011-12 as sole source, had not run the surveys of other providers the code requires, and kept sole-source contracts going past their terms because its competitions ran late.
rows.quote: “DPH extends sole source contracts beyond their initial terms”
